what: Judge orders Trump administration to return Colombian woman deported to DRC back to the US

clean_source_blocks.text: Judge called Adriana Maria Quiroz Zapata’s deportation to the Democratic Republic of Congo ‘likely illegal’ A federal judge has ordered the Trump administration to bring a Colombian woman back to the US from the Democratic Republic of Congo , after she was deported to the African country that had refused to accept her. The deportation of Adriana María Quiroz Zapata “was likely illegal”, the US district judge Richard Leon ruled on Wednesday. Continue reading...

Judge called Adriana Maria Quiroz Zapata’s deportation to the Democratic Republic of Congo ‘likely illegal’ A federal judge has ordered the Trump administration to bring a Colombian woman back to the US from the Democratic Republic of Congo, after she was deported to the African country that had refused to accept her. The deportation of Adriana María Quiroz Zapata “was likely illegal”, the US district judge Richard Leon ruled on Wednesday. Quiroz Zapata, 55, who has diabetes and a thyroid condition, “has been sent to a country that refused to accept her because they cannot provide sufficient medical care”, the ruling said. “As a result, she faces a daily risk of medical complications, up to and including death.”

Quiroz Zapata was among thousands of immigrants living legally in the US, waiting for rulings on asylum claims, when they were suddenly issued deportation decrees that ordered them expelled to countries where most had no connections. More than 15,000 third-country deportation orders were issued in the White House push for ever more immigrant expulsions, advocacy groups say, though only a fraction of the orders have been carried out. Few details are known about the agreements to accept these deportees, though the US has signed them with a range of countries, including Ecuador, Honduras, Uganda, Cameroon and the Democratic Republic of Congo. Advocacy groups estimate only a couple of hundred third-country deportations, at most, have been carried out.

Black spots began to grow on Quiroz Zapata’s back and foot while she was in detention, her skin started to peel and her nails blackened, according to a declaration that Quiroz Zapata submitted in court, and which was provided to the Associated Press by her lawyer. “She’s not doing well and does worry that she’s going to die,” her lawyer, Lauren O’Neal, said. Quiroz Zapata entered the US from Mexico in August 2024 and was taken into Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) custody. Since being deported, she has lived in a hotel in Kinshasa, the Democratic Republic of Congo’s capital. The hotel gates are locked, O’Neal said. Quiroz Zapata and other deportees are rarely allowed out, and only with supervision, she said.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: The Guardian World]
Judge called Adriana Maria Quiroz Zapata’s deportation to the Democratic Republic of Congo ‘likely illegal’

A federal judge has ordered the Trump administration to bring a Colombian woman back to the US from the Democratic Republic of Congo, after she was deported to the African country that had refused to accept her.

The deportation of Adriana María Quiroz Zapata “was likely illegal”, the US district judge Richard Leon ruled on Wednesday.

Quiroz Zapata, 55, who has diabetes and a thyroid condition, “has been sent to a country that refused to accept her because they cannot provide sufficient medical care”, the ruling said. “As a result, she faces a daily risk of medical complications, up to and including death.”

Black spots began to grow on Quiroz Zapata’s back and foot while she was in detention, her skin started to peel and her nails blackened, according to a declaration that Quiroz Zapata submitted in court, and which was provided to the Associated Press by her lawyer.

“She’s not doing well and does worry that she’s going to die,” her lawyer, Lauren O’Neal, said.

Quiroz Zapata entered the US from Mexico in August 2024 and was taken into Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) custody. Since being deported, she has lived in a hotel in Kinshasa, the Democratic Republic of Congo’s capital. The hotel gates are locked, O’Neal said. Quiroz Zapata and other deportees are rarely allowed out, and only with supervision, she said.

Quiroz Zapata was among thousands of immigrants living legally in the US, waiting for rulings on asylum claims, when they were suddenly issued deportation decrees that ordered them expelled to countries where most had no connections.

More than 15,000 third-country deportation orders were issued in the White House push for ever more immigrant expulsions, advocacy groups say, though only a fraction of the orders have been carried out.

Few details are known about the agreements to accept these deportees, though the US has signed them with a range of countries, including Ecuador, Honduras, Uganda, Cameroon and the Democratic Republic of Congo. Advocacy groups estimate only a couple of hundred third-country deportations, at most, have been carried out.

payload.title: Tuomari määräsi Trumpin hallinnon palauttamaan Kongoon karkotetun kolumbialaisnaisen Yhdysvaltoihin
payload.summary: Yhdysvaltalainen liittovaltion tuomari katsoi, että Adriana María Quiroz Zapatan karkotus Kongon demokraattiseen tasavaltaan oli todennäköisesti laiton, ja määräsi Trumpin hallinnon palauttamaan hänet Yhdysvaltoihin.
payload.content:
Yhdysvaltalainen liittovaltion tuomari on määrännyt Trumpin hallinnon tuomaan kolumbialaisen Adriana María Quiroz Zapatan takaisin Yhdysvaltoihin Kongon demokraattisesta tasavallasta. Tuomari Richard Leon katsoi keskiviikkona antamassaan ratkaisussa, että 55-vuotiaan naisen karkotus maahan, joka oli kieltäytynyt ottamasta häntä vastaan riittämättömän terveydenhoidon vuoksi, oli todennäköisesti laiton.

## Karkotus herätti huolen terveydestä

Quiroz Zapata sairastaa diabetesta ja kilpirauhassairautta. Tuomioistuimen ratkaisun mukaan hänet lähetettiin maahan, joka ei pystynyt tarjoamaan hänelle riittävää lääketieteellistä hoitoa. Ratkaisussa todettiin, että tilanteen seurauksena hänellä on päivittäinen riski vakaviin lääketieteellisiin komplikaatioihin, jopa kuolemaan.

Oikeudessa esitetyn ilmoituksen mukaan Quiroz Zapatan selkään ja jalkaan alkoi hänen säilöönottonsa aikana ilmestyä mustia läiskiä, hänen ihonsa alkoi kuoriutua ja kynnet mustuivat. Hänen asianajajansa Lauren O’Neal kuvasi naisen vointia huonoksi ja kertoi tämän pelkäävän kuolevansa.

Quiroz Zapata tuli Yhdysvaltoihin Meksikosta elokuussa 2024 ja joutui Yhdysvaltain maahanmuutto- ja tulliviranomaisten säilöön. Karkotuksen jälkeen hän on asunut hotellissa Kinshasassa, Kongon demokraattisen tasavallan pääkaupungissa. Asianajajan mukaan hotellin portit ovat lukittuina, ja Quiroz Zapata sekä muut karkotetut pääsevät ulos vain harvoin ja valvottuina.

## Osa laajempaa kolmansien maiden karkotuslinjaa

Quiroz Zapata kuului tuhansiin maahanmuuttajiin, jotka asuivat laillisesti Yhdysvalloissa ja odottivat turvapaikkahakemustensa ratkaisuja. Heille annettiin äkillisesti karkotusmääräyksiä maihin, joihin monilla ei ollut yhteyksiä.

Edunvalvontajärjestöjen mukaan Valkoisen talon pyrkimys lisätä maastapoistoja johti yli 15 000 kolmansia maita koskevaan karkotusmääräykseen. Vain pieni osa määräyksistä on toteutettu. Järjestöjen arvion mukaan tällaisia karkotuksia on tehty korkeintaan muutamia satoja.

Yhdysvaltojen kerrotaan solmineen karkotettujen vastaanottoa koskevia järjestelyjä useiden maiden kanssa. Mainittujen maiden joukossa ovat Ecuador, Honduras, Uganda, Kamerun ja Kongon demokraattinen tasavalta. Sopimusten yksityiskohdista tiedetään kuitenkin vain vähän.
